correctness.rationale: Given the published monomial-automorphism normal form for surjective 1D group cellular automata over S^m (S finite nonabelian simple), the finite coordinate permutation on (Z/NZ)x{0,...,m-1} splits by internal cycles C of length ell and drift V into g=gcd(N,V) cycles of length L=ell N/g. The automorphism accrued per full index cycle is conjugate to H_C^(N/g). Taking the t-th power splits each length-L cycle into d=gcd(t,L) components, each with monodromy H_C^((N/g)*(t/d)), giving independent fixed element choices and the exact product formula. Ordinary Möbius inversion recovers primitive periods. Equality of t=1 fixed counts with the untwisted index permutation forces each H_C^(N/g)=identity, as a fixed-point set of a finite group automorphism has full cardinality only for identity; conversely the identity holonomies permit a cyclic coordinate gauge. For nonzero V_C, each infinite index orbit is bi-infinite and admits a free gauge, yielding temporal conjugacy to full shift on S^(sum |V_C|); no spatial-shift-commuting conjugacy claimed. I independently counted 60 even permutations A5 and found centralizer of transposition (12) inside A5 has size 6, so odd/even ring one-step counts are 6/60, matching theorem. Finite example does not certify all groups; proof is arbitrary finite permutation-cycle combinatorics.

value.rationale: Periodic spatial rings are canonical finite approximants to group cellular automata; the entire temporal fixed/primitive-orbit spectrum for all ring lengths is a natural dynamical invariant not determined by topological entropy or a statement that a power is a shift. The sharp if-and-only-if finite holonomy gauge criterion and A5 odd/even obstruction versus infinite full-shift conjugacy make a mathematically motivated finite/infinite distinction.
